source_authority: The supplied first and last frames are exact endpoint authorities: a flat, thin-outlined, coarse-pixel Internet Explorer 7 style toolbar on pale pink-and-white vertical pinstripes, drawn edge to edge across the frame on a white ground. Left to right: a gold star, a green star with a white plus, one white parallelogram tab with the four-colour Windows flag and the label 'Windows Live', the short blank New Tab stub, a long empty pinstripe run, then a blue house icon with a small black triangle, an orange RSS square with a grey triangle, a grey printer with a triangle, a page icon with the word 'Page' and a triangle, a grey gear with the word 'Tools' and a triangle, and a small » chevron at the far right. The first frame has exactly ONE tab. The last frame has exactly TWO tabs: 'Windows Live' unchanged in its place and, to its right where the stub was, a second tab of identical shape and pure flat white fill with a grey page icon and the label 'Blank Page', followed by a fresh stub. The right-hand icons, their words 'Page' and 'Tools', the stars, the stripes and the bar's border lines are identical in both frames.
style_lock: the 'Windows Live' tab (Windows flag + label) is present, unchanged and in the same place in every frame; the new tab is a second tab to its right, never a replacement

the new tab is drawn EXACTLY like the first tab: pure flat white face (#FFFFFF, the same white as the first tab's face), one thin grey outline of the same weight, slanted parallelogram sides, no gradient, no gloss, no bevel, no shadow, no grey tint; if the two tab faces differ in brightness the take is wrong
the right-hand icons and the words 'Page' and 'Tools' stay exactly as they are in every frame; no new words appear anywhere except inside the new tab
the gold star, green star, pinstripes, and the bar's top and bottom border lines stay pixel-stable
coarse, crisp pixel edges as in the source; no smoothing, no repainting, no modern restyle
motion: ONE tab becomes TWO tabs, and the second tab SLIDES out from behind the first; nothing about the first tab changes. Beat 1, hold: pose one, the exact first frame, held still. Beat 2, press, about 100 ms: pose two, the small blank stub's pale face darkens slightly to a pressed tint. Beat 3, slide, about 400 ms, ease-out: a full-size second tab, identical in shape and flat white fill to the 'Windows Live' tab, already carrying the grey page icon and the label 'Connecting...', moves out from behind the 'Windows Live' tab towards the right until its left edge sits on the divider line next to the first tab; the first tab stays in front the whole time, so the second tab is progressively revealed from its right edge, and the fresh short stub rides along on the moving tab's right edge. The old stub is covered as the tab passes. Beat 4, hold: pose three, two tabs, 'Windows Live' and 'Connecting...', held perfectly still. Beat 5, swap, one frame: pose four, the label becomes 'Blank Page'; everything else unchanged. Beat 6, hold: pose four held still to the last frame. The reference video shows this exact motion on this exact toolbar; match it.
timing: Hold the first frame for the first 25 percent. The press lasts about 100 ms. The tween lasts about 400 ms with an ease-out (fast start, gentle settle) and ends by 35 percent. Hold 'Connecting...' still until about 48 percent, then swap the label to 'Blank Page' in a single frame and hold still to the end. The last frame equals the supplied last frame.
camera: Locked orthographic front view of the toolbar, framing identical to the supplied frames. No pan, zoom, roll, parallax, reframing, depth of field or vignette.
background: White ground above and below the bar, pale pink-and-white vertical pinstripes inside the bar, exactly as in the endpoint frames; perfectly still, no drift, shimmer or colour change.
